programs.notes: Five-year residence permit, renewable, without a sponsor or employer, for a foreigner who comes to the UAE as an investor or partner in a commercial project (Cabinet Resolution 65/2022, the executive regulation of Federal Decree-Law 29/2021, arts. 33(2), 38(2), 39(2) and 41; issued 12 Jul 2022, in force 3 Oct 2022). Conditions: the Federal Authority for Identity, Citizenship, Customs and Port Security (ICP) approves the investment under an investor classification system set by its chairman; the investment or partnership must reach the ratios set by a decision of the chairman (capital held in several licences is added up); and the local authority approves and licenses the activity. The regulation prints no amount and the chairman's decision is not stored, so no price is recorded. Holders may sponsor first-degree relatives, and their parents may be included. The government news agency WAM (18 Apr 2022) says it replaces an earlier investor residence valid for 2 years only; that earlier permit's start and terms are not in a stored document. launched is the in-force date of Res. 65/2022. Status active: the federal government portal (page updated 28 Jul 2026) lists investors and business partners among green visa categories, and GDRFA Dubai runs a live application service (Oct 2026). Dubai's service conditions require the investor's or partner's paid share to be at least AED 1 million, with an AED 200 entry-visa fee plus VAT; this is the Dubai condition, as the ICP chairman's federal decision is still not stored. No counts of green residence permits for investors were found.

Five-year renewable residence without a sponsor for a retired foreigner who worked at least 15 years before retiring (in or outside the UAE) or is at least 55, and who owns UAE property worth at least AED 1,000,000 (purchase or market value, as valued by the emirate's competent authority; mortgaged property counts if at least AED 1,000,000 of the mortgage has been paid off) or holds a deposit of at least AED 1,000,000, moved to a UAE financial institution within 60 days of the permit unless invested in the UAE (Cabinet Resolution 65/2022 arts. 34(3), 46, 51-52; in force 3 Oct 2022). The same article also accepts a fixed annual income of at least AED 240,000 instead of property or deposit; that option rests on income and is recorded only as one of this permit's rules (METHODOLOGY decision 15). No stored document shows whether a retiree permit existed before this regulation, so launched (the regulation's in-force date) may be later than the first retiree permit. Out of scope and not recorded: the separate residence for property owners on a monthly income of AED 10,000 with no property minimum (art. 53; decision 15). Status active: the federal government portal (page updated 28 Jul 2026) describes the retirement visa and links to live ICP and GDRFA Dubai application services. The portal words the property condition as property of AED 1 million and savings of AED 1 million (the regulation says either), and gives an income alternative of AED 180,000 a year (AED 240,000 in Dubai); both recorded as printed. No counts found.

Non-Omanis may buy built units or plots in licensed Integrated Tourism Complexes; the owner of a built unit and first-degree relatives may be granted residence (Royal Decree 12/2006 art. 8). Under the 2007 executive regulations the residence is for two years, renewed automatically every two years for six years; owners of a building plot get a two-year multiple-entry investor visa until construction is completed. No minimum price is set in the texts read. 'launched' is the decree's in-force date (date of issue, 19 Feb 2006; published 1 Mar 2006). Separate from omn-investor-residence (2021, which also has OMR 250,000/500,000 property categories under MD 58/2022). MD 109/2022 (in force 30 May 2022) rewrote art. 2 of the regulations (who may own ITC units; usufruct only in Musandam) and left the residence articles unchanged, so the system was still in force in 2022. ROP Decision 87/2026 (in force 22 Jun 2026) gives an 'owner residence' without sponsor to any foreigner owning a registered or not-yet-registered property unit, which would cover ITC owners, but it does not mention ITCs. No repeal of Royal Decree 12/2006 was found, but no current official page on ITC residence was reached (the housing ministry and ROP sites did not respond), so status is left empty. No official counts found. In scope under decision 15 (refined): buying property is in even without a minimum price; the purchase rule is recorded with the amount unset.

The 2004 Measures (MPS/MFA Order 74, approved by the State Council on 13 Dec 2003, promulgated and in force 15 Aug 2004) give permanent residence ("green card") to foreigners who have invested directly in China, with stable investment for three consecutive years and a good tax record, provided paid-in registered capital totals at least US$500,000 in encouraged sectors or in the western region and poverty counties, US$1 million in the central region, or US$2 million anywhere. Cards valid 10 years for adults; holders must spend at least 3 months a year in China. Status active: the National Immigration Administration's current service guide (dated 27 Mar 2023, online in October 2026) still lists direct and stable investment with three years of good tax records as a ground, names the 2004 Measures as its legal basis, lists the documents investors must file, and sets fees of CNY 1,500 per application and CNY 300 per card, with a decision within six months; it prints no amount, so the 2004 amounts are the latest official ones found. No official counts by route found.

Under Article 16(1)(5) of the Ministry of the Interior's regulations for Hong Kong and Macao residents (first issued 30 June 1997), a Hong Kong or Macao resident who invests NT$6 million or more in Taiwan, approved by the central competent authority, may apply for residence. Under Article 29 a resident may apply for settlement (registered permanent residence, i.e. a Taiwan household registration and ROC citizenship rights) after one year of continuous residence, or two years with at least 270 days a year, while still meeting the original conditions. Applicants who were formerly Mainland residents or who worked for Mainland party, state or military bodies may be refused (Article 22). Start: launched is 31 May 1999, the date of the full revision of the regulations (Ministry of the Interior order (88) 台內警字第 8871358 號) whose text is the earliest found with an investment ground (NT$5 million, art. 16(1)(5), plus a NT$5 million one-year deposit, art. 16(1)(6)); this date is inferred from the amendment history, since art. 16 was not amended between that revision and the 6 Aug 2001 text that is stored, and no separate in-force date is printed. The original regulations of 30 June 1997 are not in the Ministry of Justice database (historical texts start in April 2001) and were not found elsewhere, so the investment ground may be older. legal_basis is 1 July 1997, when the Hong Kong provisions of the Hong Kong and Macao Relations Act took effect; its art. 12 lets Hong Kong and Macao residents apply for residence or settlement under Ministry regulations but sets no investment ground (Macao provisions in force 20 Dec 1999). Threshold raised to NT$6 million on 10 June 2014. Status active: the current regulations (amended 13 June 2022) keep the ground. No official count of residence or settlement permits granted on the investment ground was found; the Mainland Affairs Council publishes only totals of Hong Kong residents granted residence and settlement for all reasons.

Immigration Department scheme launched 1 Sept 2022 giving wealthy foreigners a residence pass approved for 20 years (passes of 5+5+5+5 years). Status active: in October 2026 the Immigration Department's homepage links to the PVIP section of its online services portal, which offers applicant and agency registration and status inquiries, terms and conditions and an FAQ (both PDF files dated 23 Jan 2026) and a list of 50 authorised application agencies (dated 5 Oct 2026). Terms as stated in January 2026: participation fee RM200,000 for the principal (RM2,000 paid online at application, RM198,000 after approval; non-refundable) and RM100,000 per dependant (RM50,000 for a dependant who takes a 10-year approval); a fixed deposit of RM1,000,000 in a licensed Malaysian bank, of which 50% may be withdrawn after six months for property, medical or education costs; onshore and offshore income of RM40,000 a month (RM480,000 a year) or, as an alternative, a net worth of at least RM1 billion; a pass fee of RM2,000 a year plus visa fee and security bond by nationality; no age limit; children up to 25, parents and parents-in-law as dependants; extension after 20 years at half the then current participation fee; applications only through agencies registered with the Immigration Department. When the net-worth alternative, the 10-year dependant option and the six-month withdrawal rule started is not printed. The 2022 press account gave a quota of 20,000 in phase one. No official count of PVIP passes issued was found.

Separate programme run by the Sarawak Ministry of Tourism, Creative Industry and Performing Arts (Sarawak controls immigration into the state), distinct from the federal MM2H (mys-mm2h). Under the guide amended 31 Jul 2025 (rules effective 1 Jan 2025 per the minister): applicants aged 30+, a mandatory RM500,000 fixed deposit in a panel bank in Sarawak (RM250,000 minimum balance to be kept; up to 50% withdrawable after a year for a house, car, medical or education costs in Sarawak) and, in addition, a pension or offshore income of RM10,000 a month (RM15,000 with dependants) or savings of RM100,000 (RM200,000); a one-off RM5,000 processing fee; 5+5-year social visit pass; at least 30 days a year in Sarawak. Before 2025 the deposit was RM150,000 for individuals and RM300,000 for couples (as reported). Deposit plus income, like the federal MM2H. Start: launched is 2007, the earliest year in an official statement: the minister (19 Nov 2024, as reported and reposted on the ministry's site) counted 1,240 participants approved from 2007 to 2019; no founding text or launch announcement was found, so the programme may be older. The Sarawak Immigration Department ran it until the state tourism ministry took over in 2020; licensing of S-MM2H agents was delegated to Sarawak from 1 Nov 2024. Reported counts: 1,526 participants approved from 2020 to October 2024; 450 applicants with RM90 million in fixed deposits as of October 2024 (period unclear). Top nationalities since 2007 as given by the minister (China 408 applicants, UK 355, Taiwan 265, Hong Kong 260, USA 216; another statement gave China 391, UK 350) are not recorded because it is not clear whether they count applications or approvals.

The IMF (2015) describes attempts in the 1990s to sell passports, about 300 passports sold in 1996-1997 (1.5 percent of GDP in revenue), and reports of illegal issuance that led some countries, such as Canada, to drop visa waivers. Ombudsman reports give official detail on two strands: from 1993, diplomatic and official passports issued to foreigners appointed as sham honorary consuls and trade commissioners, with payments to ministers (report of 18 Mar 1998); and a "Permanent Residentship & Immigration Scheme" approved by the Council of Ministers on 19 Jun 1997 at VT 700,000 per family, sold abroad by an exclusive agent for US$15,500 to US$25,000 per person, which the Ombudsman found unlawful on 3 Dec 1997 (citizenship needs 10 years' residence under the Constitution). launched is left empty: the 19 Jun 1997 decision is the earliest official act found setting up a paid scheme, but the IMF counts passport sales already in 1996, so it does not mark the start of the sales; no official document names the scheme behind the 1996-1997 sales or its legal basis.

A 10-year residence and work permit for an applicant, spouse, dependants and household staff in return for a non-refundable USD 250,000 contribution to the COVID-19 Projects Development Fund (Immigration Act s. 9CA, inserted by the Finance (Miscellaneous Provisions) Act 2021; Immigration Act 2022 s. 14). The criteria were restated in the Finance Act 2025. Abolished by the Economic and Financial Measures (Miscellaneous Provisions) Act 2026 (Act 13 of 2026, Gazette of 13 Aug 2026), which repeals Section F of the Immigration Act 2022, the EDB Act provision for registering for the permit (s. 13(1)(b)) and Part II of the EDB Act's First Schedule (the USD 250,000 criterion); these provisions have no special commencement date, so they took effect on publication (the EDB's consolidated Act records Act 13/26 as in force 13 Aug 2026). The Act has no saving provision for existing permits. The same Act creates a 'golden visa' issued on the EDB's recommendation (USD 1 million investment; recorded separately, not as a continuation of this permit). ended is left empty: the last day applications were accepted is not stated. No figures on permits issued or money raised were found. launched is the Act's assent and Gazette date (Government Gazette No. 121 of 5 August 2021): the commencement section (s. 97) sets no other date for s. 37, so no separate in-force date is stated.

Buying qualifying residential property gives the buyer, spouse and dependants a residence permit for as long as the property is held, and the right to work or invest without an occupation permit. Threshold USD 375,000 since the Finance (Miscellaneous Provisions) Act 2020 (earlier USD 500,000 for RES, PDS and Smart City Scheme; IRS ownership gave residence with no price set in the Act as consolidated to 2009, while the Board of Investment's December 2007 IRS guidelines set IRS units at above USD 500,000 and grant the residence permit under reg. 22(1) of the IRS Regulations 2007). Senior-living PDS property above USD 200,000 for buyers over 50 since 2023. Approved by the Economic Development Board; now Immigration Act 2022 s. 8. EDB processing fee Rs 25,000 per property application (GN 69 of 2024). Start date not established: the Integrated Resort Scheme is older than the 2007 Real Estate Development Scheme Regulations (in operation 29 Nov 2007, which 'amended' the IRS and added the RES), but the original IRS regulations (reportedly 2002) and the Immigration Act amendment that first gave IRS owners resident status were not found; the Immigration Act as consolidated to 2011 shows s. 5 amended in 2002 (Act 20 of 2002, w.e.f. 1 Sep 2002), 2006, 2007, 2008 and 2009 without saying which amendment added the IRS paragraph. A path to permanent residence (20 years) exists only for other permit categories; citizenship by naturalisation normally needs 5 of 7 years' residence plus 12 months (Citizenship Act s. 9). EDB published 286 residential acquisition authorisations in FY2020/21; no count of residence permits issued under the schemes was found.

Not a citizenship-by-investment programme: requires an investment of at least USD 1 million in a Seychelles business plus 11 years' aggregate residence, a citizenship exam (80% in a national language), sponsors and public notices. Introduced by the 2013 amendments to the Citizenship Act, whose bills Cabinet approved in October 2013 (State House, 29 Oct 2013); the amending Act itself, its number and its in-force date were not obtained (SeyLII refuses automated access and its archived copies of 2013 Acts do not include it). The Immigration Department's November 2013 guide says the amendments 'will introduce' the rules, so launched is empty (decision 14; it was briefly set to the guide's month). Fee SCR 350,000 (2020 list). In November 2022 Cabinet approved further amendments to the Citizenship Act on eligibility and a public register of new citizens; whether they changed this route was not checked. The Immigration Department's current citizenship page (2026) does not mention an investor route; the current status was not part of this check. No counts found.

A residence permit category for buyers of property in the Eden Island development, listed in the Immigration Department's fee schedule (SCR 150,000 for 5 years including spouse and children). No official minimum price, legal basis or start date was found: the Immigration Regulations' fee schedule (S.I. 12 of 1981, as amended) and any agreement or regulation creating the scheme were not obtained (SeyLII refuses automated access; the government's 2007-2008 residence-permit page lists only the general discretionary permit). Industry sources cite USD 500,000 for property-linked residence permits generally, which was not confirmed officially. The ordinary residence permit is discretionary (family connection or 'special contribution' to Seychelles) and does not allow work.

Permanent residence for foreigners (with spouse and dependants) who buy built or under-construction residential property of at least EUR 80,000 in a municipality with below-average GDP per capita, or EUR 120,000 elsewhere, paid with money transferred from abroad. The card is renewed every 5 years, then every 10 after the second renewal, as long as the property is kept; property-tax and pension-income exemptions. Issued by the Direction of Foreigners and Borders (DEF). 'launched' is the in-force date: the law was published on 23 Apr 2018 and entered into force 30 days after publication (art. 13), counted from the day after publication, i.e. 23 May 2018. The implementing regulation (Decreto-Regulamentar 1/2020) took effect on 8 Jan 2020: applications go through the Casa do Cidadão as one-stop shop and DEF decides within 15 days; the Inspeção-Geral das Finanças must audit the grants yearly and publish its conclusions on the government website. Fees were set from 31 Dec 2021 (CVE 5,000; family reunification CVE 2,000; Portaria 61/2021, recast as a processing fee by Portaria 25/2022 'for the operation of the Green Card'), and the government announced in Jan 2022 that these put the Green Card into practice. Status 'active' rests on the law: the law, regulation and fee ordinances are in force, and a full-text search of the Boletim Oficial (indexed to Oct 2026) finds no repeal or suspension; a May 2024 government resolution still lists an online Green Card application among public services to digitise. No current official application page and no count of cards issued (or of the yearly audits) were found.

A foreigner who invests the prescribed financial or capital contribution in a business (or holds a ZDA investment licence, or joins an existing business with a ZDA clearance letter) can get an investor's permit (Immigration and Deportation Act 2010 s. 29, in force 17 Sep 2010); after more than three years on it he may get a residence permit (permanent residence). The Act leaves the amount to be prescribed; the Department of Immigration's current permit page (and its 2017 guide) requires proof of personal investment of US$250,000 for a new business and US$150,000 to join an existing company. No regulation setting these amounts was found. Fees: issuance 40,000 fee units under SI 113 of 2021 (from 1 Jan 2022); ZMW 16,000 issuance and ZMW 20,000 renewal since 19 Aug 2024. Status active: the department's current pages list the permit with its requirements and fees, and ZambiaLII (capture of 4 Nov 2025) shows the 2010 Act as amended in 2016 as the latest version. The separate entitlement in the ZDA Act 2006 s. 65(1) (an investor of at least USD 250,000 employing a minimum of two hundred persons, as printed, entitled to a self-employment or residence permit) ended when the Zambia Development Agency Act 2022 (Act 17, s. 23) repealed the 2006 Act with effect from 13 Jan 2023; the Investment, Trade and Business Development Act 2022, which took over investment licensing from the same date, has no immigration provision. 'launched' left empty: the ZDA Act 2006's commencement instrument is not stored (19 May 2006, the date under its long title, is kept as a 'legal' event), and the earlier Investment Act 1993 (Cap. 385, repealed by the ZDA Act 2006) and the Immigration and Deportation Act 1965 were not read, so the first text tying an investment to residence is not established. No official counts found.

The Department of Immigration issues an Investor Residence Permit on a project proposal, banking history and proof of funds available for transfer. Investment thresholds come only from a 2012 Herald article citing Zimbabwe Investment Authority procedures (US$1 million for permanent residence on application; US$300,000 sole venture or US$100,000 joint venture for a three-year residence permit leading to permanent residence); not confirmed in an official text and possibly outdated. The department's current fees page (modified 12 May 2025) charges US$500 for an investor residence permit application and US$1,000 for an investor permanent residence permit; the permits page asks US$500 plus US$300 per dependant. The Immigration Act (Cap. 4:02, 1979, as on the department's website) contains no investor provision; the investor categories presumably rest on the Immigration Regulations (SI 195 of 1998), which could not be read (ZimLII shows a bot check and no archived copy was found), so the start date is not established. No official counts found.

Run by the Sierra Leone Immigration Department with private promoters. By the promoters' account it has two parts: permanent residency through a gold bullion purchase and programme fees, and 'special naturalisation' of investors, with a company and a corporate bank account included. A press release in the Immigration Department's name (2 Jan 2025; the copy was found only on an industry site and gives a private press contact) says the GO-FOR-GOLD residency programme was launched in December 2024, and announces arrangements to naturalise high-net-worth investors and people of Sierra Leonean heritage; it gives no amounts and no legal basis. launched follows that press release; the promoters (Nov 2025) and TechCabal (2026) date the launch to January 2025. Promoters and press give USD 140,000 for the main applicant (fast-track citizenship in about 90 days), USD 100,000 on a heritage route for people of African ancestry (Jan 2025), USD 10,000-20,000 per dependant, a +1 business partner at USD 30,000 or USD 85,000 (the Nov 2025 update contradicts itself), and due-diligence fees. The promoters say citizenship is granted under the President's power in s. 27A of the Citizenship Act 1973 (legal_basis; the Act itself is not stored), that 13 families were naturalised in a six-month pilot, and that an amendment to the Act and a Citizenship (Special Naturalization) Regulation 2025 are pending; none of this was found in an official publication. Ordinary naturalisation needs 8 years' residence (15 for applicants not of Negro African descent). Current status not confirmed by a government source (the promoters said in Nov 2025 that it was active): in Oct 2026 the Immigration Department's rebuilt website (slid.gov.sl: news, notices, FAQ, fees), State House search and the archived lists of Parliament's bills and acts for 2024-2025 showed no mention of GO-FOR-GOLD, no Citizenship (Amendment) Act and no special naturalisation regulation.

UAE: both routes confirmed active from the federal portal (updated 28 Jul 2026) and live GDRFA Dubai services; Dubai sets an AED 1 million minimum share for green investors. Oman ITC: 2022 amendment found, status still unconfirmed. Jordan and Nepal start dates and India PRS status not settled. Group B of the status-asia-africa pass.
